title: Trailer for Master of Treasure
author: Fusionism
selftext: Been working on this new project for a while, a cozy collector incremental mmo with tons of skills and way gain treasure. This is the new trailer so far, still a lot of work to be done.

comments.author: AnOnlineHandle
comments.body:
The game style is nice, but I think a trap which you absolutely should try to escape is the Claude interface where everything looks like a web element with the same sort of bordering styles, shapes, fonts, etc, which are seen in so many games made with these tools and feels almost spreadsheet'y.

Have a look at what pre-existing games do differently to your UI, how they style elements and add borders etc, and then you'll have some ideas of what to aim for to escape this look which is bringing down a lot of games people are making with these tools IMO.

UI design is incredibly hard and I've been saving references for like a decade (probably at least since 2009 when I made my first proper attempt at indie game dev), and they really do help to scan over for ideas.

replies.author: Fusionism
replies.body: Yeah UI is not my strong point in game dev, ill try to improve the UI, its a heavily systems driven game and you'll have to be navigating the menus a lot of I need to put more focus on that, seems like everyone including my capsule artist seem to agree as well that the UI needs to look better.

comments.author: MeaningBoring
comments.body: game looks nice but i think you need to polish it more, UI need to be more stylized to match with the game artstyles, some object need to be have more polished art too like the boat

comments.author: TheBigQuestion354
comments.body: I would recommend at least using Tripo or Meshy for your models, every "treasure" looks super Claude.

replies.author: Fusionism
replies.body: So I made sure the 3d renderer is highly modular and adaptable, its procedurally built in game so I can easily support thousands of unique items with different properties and modifiers like stretching so they're not going to be super high quality but ill be able to do more with them, the models are generated from data there's no 3D models saved in the files. This let's me support die cracks, rotated die stamps, clipped coins, bent coins etc, if I went with real models I'd have to make multiple special variants for every single coin model in game which is just not going to work for the dynamic model system I wanted to make.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: Hmmm, it is a tough problem. Not trying to be mean, was just trying to say you would get better models with different tools but that is a conundrum.
